newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Persson calls for rapid EU expansion.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Persson calls for rapid EU expansion.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson called on Monday for a rapid expansion of the European Union to promote security and stability.

"Expanding the EU to 27 countries may be the real contribution of our generation to creating security and stability in Europe. We must not miss that opportunity," Persson said in a speech at the Olof Palme international centre.
Persson, who has championed the cause of the fledgling Baltic states in the EU, said Sweden would be highly active in the drive for a wider union.

"The EU has to live up to the expectations that have been created surrounding expansion. It must be initiated simultaneously for all countries. No country must be allowed to fall between the cracks," he said.
Persson said the parallel expansion of NATO must not be allowed to create "grey zones" as some countries found themselves excluded from both the European Union and the defence alliance.
"That would create greater uncertainty in Europe," Persson said.
